plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms that glow against dark green leaves. In the mild winter gardens of Japan, the flowers open when little else is in color. They bring welcome warmth to the coldest months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with peak bloom in midwinter
plants.location: Coastal and southern Japan, including Kyushu and the Izu Peninsula
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica has been cultivated for centuries in Japan, where it is called tsubaki. Its seeds are pressed into a prized oil used for hair care and for polishing blades.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A sprawling succulent groundcover that forms mats of fleshy leaves, topped with daisy-like flowers in vivid magenta. The petals shimmer in bright sun as if dusted with crystals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with flowering from late spring through late summer
plants.location: Highveld grasslands and rocky slopes of South Africa
plants.funFact: The shimmering look comes from tiny water-storing cells on the leaves, which give ice plants their name.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A bold wildflower with a crimson flower head that looks like a single bloom but is a cluster of hundreds of tiny flowers, ringed by showy red bracts. It stands out against the dry sandstone bushland of southeastern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly spring (September to November), with some late flowers
plants.location: Sandstone ridges and bushland around Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Its name comes from an Aboriginal word, and its nectar-rich flowers attract honeyeaters.
